body:
## Ask

Integrate vibey-gh with **Moltbook** — the reddit-style social network for AI agents — so
the automation's outputs (releases, promotions, notable merges) become Moltbook posts, and
the integration **participates in the threads it creates** rather than broadcasting into
the void.

Open naming question: does this live inside vibey-gh (it is event-driven release
automation, and releases are the natural posts), or as a sibling **vibey-moltbook** repo
that vibey-gh emits events into? Leaning sibling: vibey-gh's zero-dependency rule is
load-bearing, and a social client wants HTTP, auth, and state that don't belong here.

## Interactive, not broadcast — the hard requirement

Posting a release note is the easy 10%. The requirement is **interaction**:

- reply to comments on its own posts (human and bot commenters alike)
- answer questions about the release from the changelog/docs it already owns
- follow up when a thread surfaces a bug report — file the GitHub issue, link it back
- rate-limited, identity-labelled, and opt-in per repository, because an agent that argues
  in threads under your name is a liability, not a feature

## Fit with the existing machinery

- The local-review constrained-decoding pattern (schema-guaranteed output from a local
  model) is the right shape for reply generation: bounded, auditable, cheap.
- `workflow_run` on Release/Promote is the natural trigger — same pattern github-release.yml
  already uses.
- Config under `[moltbook]` in .vibey-gh.toml: credentials via secret, per-repo enable,
  persona/tone guardrails, hard caps on reply depth and frequency.

## Acceptance

- A release on a configured repo produces a Moltbook post within minutes, unattended.
- A comment on that post gets a grounded reply (or a deliberate, logged non-reply), never
  silence-by-crash.
- A repo without the config gets nothing — no ambient social presence.

Made-With: Vibey, the auto-vibecoding machine by Adam Matthew Steinberger

The usual cause is a request too large to complete in one attempt — several distinct changes asked for together, or a wide audit before any of them. Splitting it into separate issues, each with its own acceptance criteria, makes each one solvable. Infrastructure failures such as an exhausted API credit balance produce the same symptom; the run log distinguishes them.

Run: https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/vibey-gh/actions/runs/33122255266

Design decision, committed after tonight's doctrine wave:

Sibling repo (vibey-moltbook), not a vibey-gh feature. The zero-dependency rule is load-bearing here, and a social client wants HTTP, auth, and durable state. vibey-gh needs no changes at all: the sibling consumes GitHub release webhooks (already a first-class vibey-gh surface) as its event source — releases, promotions, and notable merges arrive as events, not polls.

Interaction architecture — the 90% this ticket is actually about — reuses infrastructure this family has already proven in production tonight:

The reply loop runs on the self-hosted vibey-local runner + Ollama with constrained decoding (the local-review fallback's exact stack): every reply is schema-constrained, grounded only in the changelog/docs/paper the release already published, with a hard "decline when the answer isn't in the sources" branch.
The same trusted-boundary rules apply: the poster credential can post and reply, never merge or push; thread content is untrusted data, never instructions.
Thread state (what was answered, budget per thread, escalation to a human) is an append-only ledger, per the pattern vibey#101 formalizes.
Scaffold lands as its own repo with the full doctrine set (arc docs, paper, book, gates) from day one — queued immediately behind the 1.50/1.52 fleet wave now landing.

Design progress — settling the open naming question in favor of the sibling repository (vibey-moltbook), for three doctrine-grounded reasons:

The zero-dependency rule is load-bearing (10.a strengthens it further): a social client needs HTTP, auth token storage, rate-limit state, and a conversation memory — none of which belong in a package that runs inside every adopter's CI. Every dependency is a party who can be pressured; vibey-gh stays clean.
Judge/actor separation (Constitution, Art. III): vibey-gh's reviewer must never share a process with an agent that argues in public threads under the maintainer's name. Separate repo, separate credential, separate blast radius.
Events are already the right interface: vibey-gh emits releases, promotions, and merges as GitHub-native facts (releases, PRs, check runs). vibey-moltbook subscribes to those — webhook or poll — and owns everything social: posting, replying from the changelog/docs corpus it indexes, filing issues back with links. vibey-gh needs zero changes beyond, later, an optional [moltbook] config block that the sibling reads from the same .vibey-gh.toml.
The hard requirement (interactive, not broadcast) maps onto machinery this family already has: constrained decoding for reply shape (the local-review pattern), a bounded reply budget per thread (the repair-budget pattern), identity-labelled machine speech (Commandments: no false witness; Art. III: labeled machine speech), and trusted_only-style gates for who it may engage. Rate limits and per-repo opt-in are config, not code paths.

Scaffolding the sibling repo is a repository-creation act — queued for the human. This ticket stays open as the integration tracker.

Made-With: Made with ❤️ by [Vibey](https://adammatthewsteinberger.github.io/vibey/), Developed by [Adam Matthew Steinberger](https://vibewithadam.matthewsteinberger.com/) ([@adammatthewsteinberger](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/)).

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Make release/promotion/merge events become Moltbook posts, and have the integration participate in its own threads — grounded replies from the changelog/docs, filing GitHub issues from bug reports surfaced in threads, rate-limited, identity-labelled, opt-in per repository.

### Evidence in the tree
- `rg -in moltbook` across the whole tree returns 6 hits and no implementation: docs/runbooks/expansion/00-master-plan.md:37 ("11 | OpenClaw / Moltbook | Not started"), 00-master-plan.md:120,142, 04-docs-scraper.md:25, 11-openclaw-moltbook.md, plus src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/templates/workflows/pr-automation.yml:382 and src/vibey_tools/gh/test/test_templates.py:572
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/templates/workflows/pr-automation.yml:382 — the only code-adjacent occurrence is a review-prompt string ("API, CLI, MCP, webhook, SDK, and Moltbook where present"), i.e. text handed to a reviewer model, not an integration
- docs/runbooks/expansion/11-openclaw-moltbook.md:3-7 — self-declared "Status (2026-09-15): not started — no `integrations/openclaw/`, no `infrastructure/moltbook/`, no `vibey moltbook` command"
- `rg -in moltbook --glob '*.toml' --glob '*.py'` — no [moltbook] table in either .vibey-gh.toml, and no Python module mentions Moltbook outside the one test assertion
- src/vibey_tools/ = {bootstrap, gh, skills}; src/vibey_runners/ = {agy, claude, codex, common, cursor, qwen} — there is no vibey-moltbook workspace tenant, and pyproject.toml:78-81 shows the workspace globs that would have picked one up automatically
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/cli.py:931-1280 — no `moltbook` subcommand among the 40+ parsers
- …and 2 more

### What is actually left
- Re-settle the placement decision, which the issue's own committed answer no longer fits: the comment of 2026-09-15 chose "sibling repo vibey-moltbook, vibey-gh needs zero changes", but ADR-0021 retired the sibling-repo model and deleted the sibling repositories. The live options are a new workspace tenant `src/vibey_tools/moltbook` or the runbook-11 design (`src/vibey/infrastructure/moltbook/` as a notify publisher). Record the choice as an ADR before writing code
- Write the Moltbook API client: POST /api/v1/agents/register, post, comment, and read-thread, with endpoints pinned to the official docs and respx-style fixture tests (no network in CI)
- Add the event source: a workflow_run trigger on Release/Promote mirroring src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/templates/workflows/github-release.yml, or a webhook consumer
- Implement the reply loop with constrained decoding against the local model, reusing the local_review.py / qwenloop pattern, with a hard "decline when the answer is not in the sources" branch grounded only in the published changelog/docs/paper
- Implement the append-only thread ledger: what was answered, per-thread reply budget, escalation to a human — the repair-budget pattern, not a fresh mechanism
- Implement the credential boundary: the poster credential may post and reply and must never merge or push; treat all thread content as untrusted data, never instructions
- Add `[moltbook]` config: per-repo enable (absent config == no ambient presence), secret-backed credentials, persona/tone guardrails, hard caps on reply depth and frequency
- Add identity labelling on every machine-authored post and reply (Art. III labelled machine speech), and keep Moltbook output out of the social-signals surface (sub-doctrine 4.a; social_signals.py renders attested human speech only)
- …and 3 more

### Blockers
- Moltbook agent registration requires a human claim step (posting a verification code on X) — operator-only, cannot be automated
- The placement decision recorded in the issue comments (sibling repo) was invalidated by ADR-0021; work cannot start until that is re-ratified
- Runbook 11 flags Moltbook post-Meta-acquisition API churn; endpoints must be pinned at build time with drift-watching, which is itself unbuilt (runbook 04)

**Notes:** Full ask is multi-week: a client, a reply loop with constrained decoding, a thread ledger, credential separation, config and guardrails, plus live human-claim verification, and the issue itself specifies the doctrine set (arc docs, paper, book, gates) from day one. A post-only MVP (release event -> one Moltbook post, no replies) is M, but the issue states explicitly that "posting a release note is the easy 10%" and that interaction is the requirement — so shipping only the MVP does not close it. Note the two competing designs in the tree pull in different directions: the issue comments want a social client outside vibey-gh reading releases as events; runbook 11 wants a notify publisher inside vibey core posting ledger DONE events. They are not the same product and should not both be built.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>
